review_comments: This changes the meaning of the test doesn't it? Why are we getting a `null` restore info here? We should only be getting that if we had a master failover in the middle of operations here shouldn't we?

@original-brownbear I think it can be null if a restore is not completed for all shards: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/snapshots/RestoreService.java#L1389
Yes but it should be completed right away because all shards should fail to restore?
But I agree it's weird, we don't check it for null almost everywhere in the snapshot tests.

@original-brownbear  I looked at it deeper, all the test failures happen due to the cluster turning RED via `desiredBalance`
```
[2023-02-21T22:36:59,495][INFO ][o.e.c.r.a.AllocationService] [node_s0] current.health="RED" message="Cluster health status changed from [YELLOW] to [RED] (reason: [reconcile-desired-balance])." previous.health="YELLOW" reason="reconcile-desired-balance"
```

I believe the issued got fixed in #93635. This is also corroborated by the fact that the test fails only in 7.6 and 7.7.
I'm not sure if need this null check or it would be better to add an `ensureGreen` assertion before mounting a snapshot
